ctx.x: Duke is because I figured Duke was never paying enough. I would've loved to work with Duke, but I didn't think Duke was going to pay me no two-fifty or three. Those other bands -- those other tenor players, you know, working in those big white bands, they was getting like five hundred dollars a week. And Duke here paying these guys two-fifty.

items.title: 68251_Teddy McRae oral history interview
items.q: Artie Shaw was funny... And Georgie Auld say, 'Man, you're' ... Artie came to me and say, 'Look, this' -- he rehearsed with that band. ... That's when he Georgie Auld. A few of the other trombone players came in there, (inaudible), put some other men in his band.

ctx.x: MR. WELBURN: This is Huntington and Massachusetts Avenue.

Yeah. That's where the -- you know, where the Boston Pop up there. Now they got an underpass. Massachusetts Avenue ... it's a (Inaudible) building, (Inaudible) Traffic Jam. We had rehearsal and Boston Pop was breaking one day. Man, you couldn't get across the street nowhere. People come out all out in the street. I said, "This is a traffic jam." So Artie said, "When you're gonna write for me?" I say, "I gotta think first." And always would show him a piece of paper about like eight bars, you know. And that would…
